outcome: conformity of indications and implementation of UFPM
maternal adverse events (laceration of the birth canal, cervical laceration, uterine rupture, severe AEs, maternal deaths)
fetal adverse events (admission to neonatal intensive care unit, sequela)
cohort: The study included 265 patients who underwent uterine fundal pressure maneuver (UFPM) between January 2015 and March 2017.
finding: The study found that 95.7% of UFPM cases were compliant with guidelines, with birth canal laceration being the most frequent maternal adverse event, and 12.5% of newborns requiring NICU admission, though all developed normally without sequela.
mod_finding: The findings showed that maternal adverse events such as birth canal laceration and cervical laceration were observed following UFPM during the second stage of labor to facilitate vaginal delivery.
